title: Qatar shuts down, deregisters several non-compliant travel and air cargo agencies
summary: Qatar's Civil Aviation Authority closed two travel and air cargo agencies and deregistered 10 others after inspections found regulatory breaches. The QCAA warned agencies to stop operating without proper licenses and cited Article (3) of Law No. (3) of 2025, emphasizing strengthened oversight of the air transport sector.
content:
Doha, Qatar: The Qatar Civil Aviation Authority (QCAA), represented by the Air Transport Department, ordered the administrative closure of two travel and air cargo agencies and de-registration of 10 others for non-compliance.

The actions came after inspection campaigns aimed at ensuring agencies comply with approved laws and regulations governing air transport and related services. The violations were identified during these oversight activities, prompting the QCAA to take immediate administrative measures.

The QCAA reaffirmed its commitment to enhancing inspection activities across the sector and urged all agencies to fully comply with the regulatory framework. It warned companies to refrain from conducting any travel or air cargo-related activities without obtaining the necessary licenses from the competent department, in accordance with the provisions of Article (3) of Law No. (3) of 2025.

Officials said the closures and de-registrations are part of ongoing efforts to strengthen oversight, regulate the air transport sector more effectively, and protect consumers and industry standards. Agencies found operating without proper authorization or failing to meet statutory requirements will face sanctions until they meet compliance conditions.

The QCAA emphasized that further inspection campaigns and enforcement measures will continue as it seeks to ensure safe, lawful, and transparent operations within Qatar's travel and air cargo markets.
